problem_summary.summary: Combine every group of overlapping closed intervals and return sorted, non-overlapping intervals covering the same points.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: intervals as [start, end] pairs in arbitrary order. Return merged [start, end] pairs in ascending start order.
constraints: Intervals sharing an endpoint count as overlapping

brute_force.explanation: Insert each interval into a sorted list built so far. Scan to its insertion point, absorb every interval whose start is no greater than the growing end, and insert the combined interval.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The maintained list is sorted and pairwise non-overlapping. The scan finds exactly the entries intersecting the inserted closed interval; merging their minimum start and maximum end preserves coverage and restores the invariant.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2) in the worst case because insertion, removal, and scanning may each shift or inspect O(n) list entries for each input interval.

optimized.explanation: Sort intervals by start, then scan once. Extend the last output interval when the next start is at most its end; otherwise append a new interval.
optimized.correctness_idea: After sorting, any interval that can overlap the current merged interval must appear next. Extending the end absorbs all such intervals; a strict gap proves the current merged interval is complete.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n log n) for sorting plus O(n) for the scan.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) for the merged output; Java's object-array sort may also use O(n) temporary storage.

steps.condition: Intervals are now in ascending start order.
steps.action: Initialize output with the first interval.
Extend the last end to max(3, 6).

edge_cases.handling: The <= overlap test merges them, as required for closed intervals.
The maximum end keeps the containing interval unchanged.
Every sorted interval is appended as its own output range.
